sections.heading: 1. Three comeback rules
lines: ① Weeks 1–2: about half your usual load.
② Clearly worse 24 hours later? Drop a step.
③ Add weight, sets or sessions, not all three.

slides.title: Check before you push on
slides.bubble:
Causes differ for everyone.
An assessment comes first!
slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Lulu is back at the gym after a month off with his ankle, and his ego is already loading the bar.

Most people do well starting at about half their usual weights and volume for the first week or two, then building up gradually. Mild discomfort during a set is often fine; the next-morning check tells you more. If things are clearly worse 24 hours later, drop back a step.

Change one thing at a time, and keep training the parts that aren't injured. Swelling that keeps returning, a joint that gives way or numbness is worth getting checked.

Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can map out a return that fits your program. Book online via the link in bio 🏋️
